questions.q: WHERE Id IN (SELECT AccountId FROM Opportunity WHERE StageName = 'Closed Won') on Account is an example of what pattern?
questions.explain: A semi-join uses IN with a subquery to keep records that have a match — here, accounts with at least one closed-won opportunity.

questions.q: What does an anti-join (NOT IN with a subquery) return?
options: Records that have NO matching counterpart in the subquery's results
Records that have at least one matching counterpart in the subquery
Only records from the subquery's object
Records sorted by how many matches they have
questions.explain: NOT IN with a subquery is the inverse of a semi-join — it keeps only records with zero matches in the subquery's result set.

questions.q: What is the documented limit on IN/NOT IN statements per WHERE clause in a semi-join or anti-join query?
questions.explain: SOQL documents a limit of at most two IN or NOT IN statements per WHERE clause.

questions.q: What field type must the main query filter on for a semi-join or anti-join?
options: A single ID (primary key) or reference (foreign key) field
questions.explain: The main query's left operand in a semi-join or anti-join must be a single ID or reference field — not an arbitrary field type.

questions.q: Why is writing NOT (Id IN (subquery)) problematic?
options: It silently returns zero rows every time
It is a syntax error that SOQL always rejects
NOT can't be used as a simple conjunction here — it effectively flips a semi-join into an anti-join rather than acting as plain negation
It is identical in every way to writing NOT IN directly, so there's no issue
questions.explain: SOQL documents that NOT cannot be used as a conjunction with semi-joins and anti-joins — using it this way converts the join type rather than negating it generically, so the anti-join should be written directly as NOT IN.
